Article Title: UN approves resolution to declare Nov 27 as ‘International Day For Elimination Of Child, Early & Forced Marriage’
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a significant development that brings focus on the need to step up action to deliver on the Sustainable Development Goals 2030, the United Nations (UN) has declared November 27 the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. The date carries special significance for India, which backed the resolution steered by Sierra Leone, as it was on Nov 27 that the govt had launched the ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat’ campaign in 2024.Even though underage marriage has been declining over the decades, the numbers are still a concern calling for greater efforts to eradicate the problem. According to the 2019-21 National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 23.3% of women aged 20-24 were married before the age of 18. This came down to 20.1% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).Just Rights for Children founder Bhuwan Ribhu, who has been vociferously advocating for a dedicated day and has worked closely with the drafting of the resolution, said that the announcement is very significant for India as it is an opportunity to lead by example and meet the elimination targets.Welcoming the UN approval for the demand from countries across the world, Ribhu said, “Today marks the tipping point, showing that the end of the crime of child marriage is inevitable and imminent.Now is the time for governments globally to provide decisive leadership to end child marriage by 2030 and ensure education, protection and development of every child to realise their full potential. I am grateful to the First Lady of Sierra Leone for her leadership in championing this cause and would also like to thank the countries that co-sponsored our resolution. “ He was present at the UN as the civil society representative when the UN approved the resolution.“The Government of India has set a target of reducing the prevalence of child marriage by 10% by 2026. With continued efforts at the national and state levels, the prevalence of child marriage in India is expected to fall below 15% by the end of 2026. The global commitment to eliminate child marriage by 2030 is aligned with target 5.3 of Sustainable Development Goal 5 (Gender Equality), which calls for the elimination of all harmful practices, including child, early, and forced marriage,” Ribhu added.He shared that plans are afoot to hold extensive outreach campaigns in coordination with the govt and states ahead of November 27 to ensure that the day becomes a space to dwell on progress made and the way forward and does not end up as a symbolic reminder of the problem.
Article Summary: The UN has declared November 27 the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. The date carries special significance for India, which backed the resolution steered by Sierra Leone. It was on Nov 27 that the govt had launched the ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat’ campaign.

Article Title: ‘Will be compelled to launch large-scale agitation’: Sonam Wangchuk ahead of Ladakh talks with Centre
Article Text:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk (PTI photo)

NEW DELHI: Ladakh-based activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday said the Leh Apex Body (LAB) would be compelled to launch a “very large-scale agitation” if the Union government fails to make “concrete” progress on the group’s key demands.“If stepmotherly treatment is meted out to Ladakh and the people living along the borders, then we will be compelled to launch a very large-scale agitation after September 9,” PTI quoted him as saying. He was referring to the date when an LAB sub-committee is scheduled to meet Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) officials in Delhi to press for its demands.Wangchuk further announced that the outfit's proposed march from Kargil to Leh, scheduled to begin on September 10, had been postponed in view of the MHA talks. However, he warned the march would be revived if the talks fail to produce a “satisfactory” outcome.“We have collectively decided to postpone the 'padyatra' for the time being. We will once again appeal to people from across India to come forward in support of Ladakh, in support of the environment, and in support of the people of Ladakh who remain steadfast on the country's borders,” he stated.He added that the LAB is observing September as “Martyrs' Month” in memory of those killed, injured and jailed last year.The activist was referring to the violence in Leh, the Union territory's capital, on September 24 last year, during which four civilians were killed, allegedly in police firing. Wangchuk himself was detained under the stringent National Security Act and released six months later, in March this year.Wangchuk, who emerged as the face of the recent student protests in Delhi and sat on a hunger strike for more than 20 days, also said the LAB expects the Centre to bring a detailed draft on the proposed Ladakh assembly, including its powers and rights, to the September 9 meeting.The outfit has been demanding legislation for Ladakh at the Union territory level, safeguards under Article 371, withdrawal of cases filed after the September 24 violence last year, compensation for victims and publication of the inquiry commission report. The LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) have been jointly spearheading the agitation since Ladakh was granted Union territory status in August 2019 and have held several rounds of talks with the Centre since 2021.
Article Summary: Ladakh-based activist Sonam Wangchuk said the Leh Apex Body (LAB) would be compelled to launch a “very large-scale agitation” if the Union government fails to make “concrete” progress on the group’s key demands. He was referring to the violence in Leh, the Union territory's capital, on September 24 last year.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu's Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) on Saturday conducted searches at the residence and premises linked to DMK leader and former minister KN Nehru in connection with alleged irregularities in the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department.The searches were conducted in Thillai Nagar, Tiruchirappalli.DMK cadres gathered outside Nehru's residence during the searches. Former minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi also visited Nehru's home.The case relates to allegations of corruption in recruitment, contract allocation and transfers during Nehru's tenure as the minister in charge of the department.The DVAC registered an FIR after the Madras high court directed it to initiate a probe into allegations related to the department. The agency named Nehru, his relatives and several officials as accused.The allegations include a Rs 888-crore cash-for-jobs scam, in which money was allegedly collected from candidates in exchange for government jobs, as well as irregularities in contracts worth around Rs 1,020 crore and illegal transfers and postings linked to the department.The Enforcement Directorate (ED) had earlier shared details of the alleged irregularities with Tamil Nadu authorities, following which the matter came under scrutiny.However, the Madras high court later granted an interim stay on further action by the vigilance agency and proceedings against the accused. Legal proceedings in the matter are continuing.
Article Summary: The case relates to allegations of corruption in recruitment, contract allocation and transfers during Nehru's tenure as the minister in charge of the department. Article Title: Coal stock at thermal plants plummets, 'critical' at 50 units
Article Text:
Coal stocks at thermal power plants across the country have fallen to less than half the recommended level

Of the 50 plants, 45 are based on domestic fuel

Poll Vote & Share your view How would you rate the information provided by the coal ministry regarding coal stock levels? Very informative Not informative 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Coal stocks at thermal power plants across the country have fallen to less than half the recommended level, with 50 plants classified as having 'critically low' inventories as on Sept 2 amid high electricity demand and monsoon-led disruptions in supplies, Central Electricity Authority data showed.The plants, with a combined capacity of around 224 GW, had 28.2 million tonnes (MT) of coal as of Wednesday, 48% of the prescribed requirement of 58.7 MT. The available stock is equivalent to about nine days of coal requirement at 85% plant load factor, against the normal requirement of around 19 days.The plants classified as short on coal stocks have less than 25% of their normative inventories. Coal ministry officials, however, said all critical plants were being monitored by an inter-ministerial team of officials on a day-to-day basis and regular fuel supplies were being provided to them.Of the 50 plants, 45 are based on domestic fuel, four are designed for imported coal and one runs on washery rejects.A senior coal ministry official said, "Classification of a thermal power plant as critical is a routine monitoring parameter under norms laid down by CEA. It simply means closer tracking and priority action. These plants are not running out of supply."Though the normative coal requirement at power plants is calculated at 3.1 MT every day at 85% plant load factor, officials said the actual requirement is around 2.4 MT.The monsoon sees supply disruptions every year. The situation starts improving from Sept onwards as rains begin to recede.While the power ministry did not respond to requests for a reaction, sources said some coal-fired plants had been asked to defer scheduled maintenance to ensure continuity of electricity generation.
Article Summary: Coal stocks at thermal power plants across the country have fallen to less than half the recommended level. 50 plants classified as having 'critically low' inventories as on Sept 2. High electricity demand and monsoon-led disruptions in supplies blamed.

Article Title: Europe waking up to Modi's warning 'a bit late': Belgian PM
Article Text:
Belgian PM said India and Europe were now facing similar challenges

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever on Friday said Europe had been slow to recognise the risks of becoming too dependent on other economies, admitting that Indian PM Narendra Modi had warned it about the problem much earlier but was not heard.De Wever, who was on a two-day visit to India to strengthen ties in trade, investment, technology and strategic cooperation, said India and Europe were now facing similar challenges as economic dependencies were increasingly being used as leverage. "We do not like dependencies becoming weaponised against us. You have lived this history. Your Prime Minister warned Europe about this long time ago already. But he was ignored. He wasn't listened to. We are listening now," De Wever said at a Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) event.Calling Europe's awakening "a bit late", De Wever said the region was now having the "right debates" about who it could work with in a world where major economic powers were moving in different directions.He said India was the most important partner for Europe among countries that believed in multilateralism and cooperation based on "respect and not force"."If India is not on the list, then you have missed something fundamental. India is on that list. It's number one," De Wever said.In an apparent reference to China, De Wever said Europe was seeking to reduce its dependence on "big economical powerhouses" that were moving away from rules-based cooperation. "I will not name them China," he said, adding that such a direction was not what Europe wanted.Speaking on the occasion, Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal said the India-EU FTA was a win-win for everyone. "It will open opportunities for farmers, start ups, women entrepreneurs, it has something for everyone. It's been deftly negotiated protecting sensitive sectors on both sides. It offers huge potential for both sides," he said.
Article Summary: Belgian PM Bart De Wever on a two-day visit to India to strengthen ties in trade, investment, technology and strategic cooperation. He said India and Europe were now facing similar challenges as economic dependencies were increasingly being used as leverage. "We do not like dependencies becoming weaponised against us. Article Title: SC awards pension to Mumbai engineer who forged ST certificate
Article Text:
SC allowed him to superannuate in peace with retirement benefits

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has rewarded a wrongdoer - a man who got appointed as a junior civil engineer in Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) by producing a forged ST certificate, and, subsequently, stalled the scrutiny of his eligibility for quota for more than a decade - by allowing him to superannuate in peace with retirement benefits.Shirish P Patil got a certificate in 1984 by identifying himself as belonging to the 'Tokre Koli' Scheduled Tribe community. Based on the certificate, he was appointed a junior civil engineer in MCGM in 1994. He misplaced the original ST certificate but managed to secure a fresh one from the sub-divisional magistrate, Bhusawal division, in Oct 2000.Following scrutiny initiated by MCGM, the Police Vigilance Cell traced Patil's family history and found that his ancestors had been recorded as 'Koli', 'Hindu Koli' and 'Hindu Suryawanshi Koli', none of which belonged to the ST category. In July 2009, MCGM issued a show cause notice to Patil.He successfully dodged and delayed proceedings before the scrutiny committee until Jan 2020, when the panel rejected his plea that his lawyer and elderly family members were not available, and invalidated the ST certificate. HC dismissed his appeal against cancellation of ST status.SC, however, stayed Patil's dismissal from service through an interim order on Nov 18, 2021.As a result, the engineer continued to serve until June 30, 2025, when he retired after being employed with MCGM for more than three decades based on a forged ST certificate.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi Thursday upheld the cancellation of Patil's ST certificate and Bombay HC order. However, it took a lenient view given his undertaking that he or any of his family members "shall (not) be entitled to claim any future benefit on the basis of the invalidated ST certificate".The ruling contrasts with SC's consistent rulings against benefits accruing to people who forge SC or ST certificates to gain admission or employment.
Article Summary: Shirish P Patil got a certificate in 1984 by identifying himself as belonging to the 'Tokre Koli' Scheduled Tribe community. Based on the certificate, he was appointed a junior civil engineer in MCGM in 1994. In July 2009, MCGM issued a show cause notice to Patil. He successfully dodged and delayed proceedings before the scrutiny committee.

Article Title: Amazon techie leaves Rs 46 lakh package to join Indian Army, set to be commissioned at OTA Gaya
Article Text:
Shardendu Tiwari





LUCKNOW: Lucknow’s 27-year-old Shardendu Tiwari, who worked as a cloud engineer at Amazon with an annual package of around Rs 46 lakh, is set to be commissioned into the Army at the Officers Training Academy (OTA), Gaya, on Saturday.A second-generation soldier, Shardendu chose military service after leaving behind a corporate career and an opportunity with global aerospace company Airbus. His commissioning will mark the culmination of his journey from the technology sector to the armed forces.Shardendu resides in Neelmatha, Lucknow, and his family traces its roots to Pipergaon in Sultanpur district. His father, Honorary Captain Raj Kumar Tiwari, served in the Army Service Corps for 36 years before retiring. Inspired by his father, Shardendu developed an inclination towards joining the armed forces during his childhood.He completed his schooling at Kendriya Vidyalaya, Chandimandir, Haryana. He pursued a Bachelor of Engineering degree in Information Technology and later completed an MTech in Computer Science and Information Security from Punjab Engineering College, Chandigarh.Shardendu appeared for Army selection eight times before succeeding.He joined through the technical entry route, which enabled him to serve in the Army while remaining connected with technology.“I was also drawn to the armed forces because of the opportunities they offer for adventure and field service,” he said.During training at OTA Gaya, his leadership qualities earned him the appointment of Senior Under Officer (SUO), one of the highest cadet appointments at the academy. He enjoys playing basketball and table tennis.
Article Summary: Shardendu Tiwari, 27, is set to be commissioned into the Army at the Officers Training Academy (OTA), Gaya, on Saturday. His commissioning will mark the culmination of his journey from the technology sector to the armed forces. Shardendu chose military service after leaving behind a corporate career and opportunity with global aerospace company Airbus.

Article Title: Hours after AAIB report, AI sacks Phuket flight pilot
Article Text:
Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi

Software malfunction or manual intervention? Final report may reveal

NEW DELHI: Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight hours after Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report concluded the "PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory (dope) test". Terming this confirmation a "serious concern", AAIB has asked Directorate General of Civil Aviation to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance" on "priority" in its interim safety recommendations and conclusion. Aviation secretary Samir Sinha had soon after this accident asked DGCA chief Vir Vikram Yadav to make dope rules more stringent.AI was considering action, including termination, against the PIC for some weeks now but was awaiting AAIB's prelim report into what has now been categorised as an "accident" due to its severity and impact. An AI spokesperson said: "Safety remains AI's highest priority. In line with AI's zero-tolerance approach to violation of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements, the pilot's employment has been terminated with immediate effect. "When the badly rattled Airbus A320 had landed in Delhi with 24 injured people and a damaged aircraft cabin, both the pilots were subjected to post-flight breath-analyser examination as per standard protocol.They cleared that test.But for some reason which may be disclosed in the final report, the unusual step of conducting dope tests was taken in this case. “The sample of PIC was found non-negative. Blood samples of both the flight crew were sent to path lab for confirmatory (dope) test. The confirmatory test report of PIC was found non-negative whereas the sample of co-pilot was found negative in both the tests,” stated the interim report.An AAIB probe is on to find what caused the Airbus A320 to suffer an extremely rare failure of all three hydraulic systems within seconds. The final report is expected to reveal whether it happened due to something going wrong with the aircraft’s hardware or software or whether due to some manual intervention with the PIC having some role in that, if any. Hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheels.Such was the impact of this “event” which happened that 24 people got injured and the aircraft cabin saw significant damage, including a lavatory commode getting uprooted from its location. The overhead ceiling panel was found cracked or deformed at various places. Most of the passenger service unit panels were found dislocated or bent at various places. The overhead handrail was found broken and sealing panel found dislocated near the tenth row. The forward right side emergency exit handle was found broken.The cabin supervisor (head cabin crew) apprised the cockpit about the injuries suffered by the passengers and crew. The crew assessed the cabin situation and took the decision of continuing the flight to its destination Delhi and not diverting to the nearest en route airport.Following the report, AI said: “We acknowledge the release of the preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau and continue to extend our full cooperation to the investigation, including providing access to all relevant operational, maintenance and technical records. Safety remains Air India’s highest priority. Our pilots undergo rigorous training, regular proficiency checks, medical examinations and other regulatory assessments in accordance with applicable national and international requirements. Following the incident, Air India has started voluntary testing of 100% of its pilots as a further step to reinforce its safety-first approach.” “The airline maintains zero tolerance for any breach of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements,” Air India’s statement added.
Article Summary: Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket- Delhi flight. Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report concluded the "PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory (dope) test" AAIB has asked Directorate General of Civil Aviation to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit"

Article Title: Ladakh residents to get ownership rights over 60,000 acres of barren land
Article Text:
Ladakh residents will now have rights over barren lands or wastelands owned by govt

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Ladakh residents will now have rights over barren lands or wastelands owned by govt, with the administration Friday approving Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Nautor Regularisation) Rules, 2026.The Rules provide a comprehensive framework for granting proprietary rights on up to 10 acres of eligible Nautor land holdings to the occupants across all seven districts of the Union Territory. For Nautor land beyond the 10-acre limit, the proprietary rights may be allotted on a leasehold basis, in accordance with the rules.Nautor land refers to barren or wasteland, owned by govt, which was earlier allotted to individuals for cultivation or other productive use. More than 60,000 acres of land in Ladakh is presently recorded in revenue records as Nautor holdings.The Rules offer a one-time regularisation mechanism for Nautor land, occupied before the repeal of J&K Tenancy Act-980, on Oct 27, 2020. Any possession of Nautor land after this cut-off date will be ineligible for regularisation.“The Nautor issue has a deep historical connection with the lives and livelihoods of the people of Ladakh.For generations, our people have worked hard to bring barren and waste land under cultivation in one of the most challenging agricultural environments in the country. These Rules provide a transparent and uniform mechanism to address this long-pending issue and give legal certainty to genuine holders. It will also enable such land to be utilised as a financial asset, including for availing bank loans,” Ladakh LG Vinai Kumar Saxena said.According to the Rules, the authority of allotting Nautor land will be vested in Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils in all seven districts.A govt spokesperson said the absence of a clear and uniform legal framework until now restricted the effective utilisation of Nautor land. “In particular, landholders with limited or non-proprietary rights, were unable to use the land as a financial asset, including for purposes such as obtaining loans against it. At the same time, the absence of uniform rules also posed a threat of claims and disputes over govt, council land,” the spokesperson said.
Article Summary: Ladakh residents will now have rights over barren lands or wastelands owned by govt. Administration Friday approving Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Nautor Regularisation) Rules, 2026. Rules provide a comprehensive framework for granting proprietary rights on up to 10 acres of eligible Nautor land holdings.

Article Title: Punjab government to hike DA of 85,000 employees from 42 to 60 pc: Minister Aman Arora
Article Text:
Punjab government will raise the Dearness Allowance of around 85,000 government employees

Chandigarh, Punjab government will raise the Dearness Allowance of around 85,000 government employees recruited after July 17, 2020 by 18 per cent to 60 per cent, Cabinet Minister Aman Arora said on Friday.Speaking to mediapersons here, Arora said a recommendation in this regard was made by the Cabinet Sub-Committee formed to examine the issues of employees.The announcement is significant as employees recruited after July 17, 2020 were getting a pay equivalent to the Central pay scales, along with 42 per cent Dearness Allowance (DA). These were much lower than the pay scales of employees recruited before July 2020, who were paid as per the Punjab Pay Commission.Arora said there were two pay scales in Punjab, which was leading to conflicting interests and confusion: the Punjab basic pay scales and the one equivalent to the Central basic pay scales (as per the 7th Central Pay Commission)."Punjab basic pay scales, which traditionally are higher, range from 30 to 70 per cent more than the Central basic pay. And when DA is added to it, which is currently 42 per cent, the salary increases much above the Central pay scales," he said."When we calculate and compare, even with 60 per cent DA added to Central basic pay, the Punjab pay scales and take-home salaries are higher," he said.Arora said the previous Congress government had decided to hire employees on the Central pay scales after July 17, 2020.In the last six years, 85,000 employees have been recruited.The Mann government will give them a "Janmashtami gift" as the three-member Cabinet Sub-Committee has decided that the DA of these employees will be raised from 42 to 60 per cent. The committee's recommendation will be sent to the chief minister, Arora said.He, however, said that this hike will not benefit employees recruited before July 2020."From day one, the Bhagwant Mann government has been talking about the welfare of every section. We cannot imagine good governance without our employees," he said.The development comes amid over 3 lakh government employees, who went on a statewide strike on August 27, pressing the state government to accept their various demands, including the release of their pending 18 per cent DA.They have also threatened to go on mass casual leave on September 8 if the state government does not withdraw a recent notice imposing disciplinary action against those who remained on "unauthorised absence" on August 27.The employees have given the state government time till September 7 to withdraw the notice issued to protesting employees.Punjab government on Thursday appealed to employee unions to engage with it through dialogue rather than confrontation, calling employees the backbone of good governance.
Article Summary: Punjab government will raise the Dearness Allowance of around 85,000 government employees recruited after July 17, 2020 by 18 per cent to 60 per cent, Cabinet Minister Aman Arora said on Friday. The development comes amid over 3 lakh government employees, who went on a statewide strike on August 27.

Article Title: Smoking raises mortality risk by 55% for diabetics
Article Text:
Smoking raises mortality risk by 55% for diabetics

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes, according to evidence reviewed in a new international consensus that calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type-2 diabetes care. Experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-ups instead of being given a one-time "quit smoking" warning.The recommendations, published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, represent the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type-2 diabetes. They were developed by 35 experts from 13 countries, including Indian diabetes specialist Dr Anoop Misra.The consensus recommends varenicline as the first-line medicine where available, with nicotine replacement therapy or bupropion as alternatives when varenicline is unavailable or unsuitable. Medicines should be combined with structured, intensive behavioural support and repeated contact rather than brief counselling alone.The stronger approach reflects the added risk smoking poses to people with diabetes.A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.Doctors should review patients within two weeks of their quitting and again at four weeks, checking blood sugar, weight, blood pressure and medicines, as quitting can alter drug metabolism and sometimes require dose adjustments.Smoking is also linked to kidney damage in diabetics, with higher risks of albuminuria and diabetic nephropathy. A Japanese study of 2,490 people with type-2 diabetes found insulin resistance rose with cigarettes smoked per day and fell with time after quitting.Quitting, however, can be difficult. Some patients may not recognise the link between smoking and diabetes complications, while others fear weight gain or use cigarettes to cope with stress and anxiety. The experts recommend personalised quitting strategies and relapse prevention.
Article Summary: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes. New international consensus calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type-2 diabetes care. Experts say patients should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-ups.

Article Title: PMLA court: Cheques, drugs constitute proceeds of crime
Article Text:
The judge convicted two accused and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years

NEW DELHI: Broadening the definition of "property" under Prevention of Money Laundering Act, a special PMLA court in Mohali has ruled that seized bank cheques, even if not encashed, and narcotics both fall under the definition of "property" and constitute proceeds of crime under the money laundering Act.The judgement came Thursday, when ED launched a massive search operation at 30 premises across all zones of the southern region in different narcotics-related cases. The searches are being conducted under the mandate of Centre's 'Nasha Mukt Bharat' campaign with targets in the first phase spread across Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.The judge convicted two accused and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years, while rejecting the contention of the defence that their property and bank accounts were not attached and the seized contraband could not be considered proceeds of crime as no money trail had been brought on the record.Special judge Hardip Singh also rejected the defence's argument that the cheques recovered from the accused were not encashed and thus could not constitute proceeds of crime. The judge noted that the cheques were exchanged for the purpose of purchasing the contraband and the accused could not provide any explanation to the contrary.Starting with the four southern states, ED Thursday began a crackdown on major drug syndicates operating across the country.The drive has been launched as part of Centre's "drug-free India" campaign to attach properties of all those engaged in drug dealing and generation of "proceeds of crime". The ED's search covered targets involved in trafficking of illicit drugs like methamphetamine, marijuana, and MDMA. Over 20 foreign nationals are under scanner, an official said.Searches were conducted at premises in Chennai, Tirunelveli, Nagapattinam, Velankanni and Ramanathapuram in Tamil Nadu; Kolar, Malur (Kolar district) and Hoskote (Bengaluru North district); Serilingampally and Nanakramguda (Hyderabad) and Ranga Reddy district in Telangana; Kozhikode, Kannur, Malappuram and Thrissur in Kerala.ED is coordinating with other central agencies and state police forces that have registered cases of drug trafficking in the past few years to further investigate the money trail and track the proceeds of crime."The investigation prima facie discloses not merely trafficking of methamphetamine, but also the generation, receipt and movement of money arising out of this," a senior official said, adding that syndicates were using hawala and crypto currency dealers to further transfer the proceeds of crime outside the country to tax havens.The money trail to uncover cash-based hawala settlements revealed "account details, transaction records, diaries, slips or tokens, mobile phones, electronic communications and digital devices, property documents and other financial records". Based on these findings, the agency ascertained the complete quantum and trail of the proceeds of crime, and the persons who received, possessed, transferred, concealed, utilised or invested such proceeds.Further these details help in identifying movable and immovable properties acquired and that leads to their attachments.
Article Summary: A special PMLA court in Mohali has ruled that seized bank cheques, even if not encashed, and narcotics both fall under the definition of "property" The judgement came Thursday, when ED launched a massive search operation at 30 premises across all zones of the southern region in different narcotics-related cases. The judge convicted two accused and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years.

Article Title: Dog bite ordeal doesn’t end with rabies prophylaxis
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: For a 21-year-old Delhi resident bitten by a stray dog, the ordeal did not end after he received rabies post-exposure prophylaxis. Within seven days, he developed a skin rash that progressed to severe hives (urticaria) and angioedema, causing sudden swelling of the face, lips and throat. His condition later worsened with breathing difficulty, requiring specialist dermatological intervention.The case comes against the backdrop of the Supreme Court’s May 2026 directions on the stray-dog menace, which stressed the need to protect people from dog attacks and strengthen measures for sterilisation, vaccination and dog-bite management.The young man was bitten over two weeks ago and was initially taken to a Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) centre, where he received equine immunoglobulin (IgG) and a rabies vaccine.He was later taken to Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital. After two days of treatment, when he developed difficulty breathing, he was evaluated by the dermatology department.Doctors advised a single injection of omalizumab to control the severe allergic reaction. The medicine cost around Rs 16,000-17,000. The family was advised to explore obtaining it through the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS), but the patient’s mother, Rama (name changed), bought it herself, worried about her son’s condition.The patient improved within 24 hours of receiving omalizumab and remains under treatment at RML Hospital.Dr Kabir Sardana, who treated the patient in the dermatology department, said he sees around one such case a week and believes this could be the first reported use of omalizumab for this type of reaction following rabies prophylaxis. The treatment was given after the option was discussed with the family and with their concurrence.Sardana said it can sometimes be difficult to distinguish whether a rash is due to the vaccine or immunoglobulin, as both early and delayed reactions can occur. “The aim is to maximise treatment, minimise discomfort and, of course, see the financial aspects of the patient,” he said.The episode also highlighted the financial burden of managing severe reactions. “Every patient cannot afford Rs 17,000. What can poor people do? They are suffering so much,” Rama said.More broadly, he said, adverse reactions following rabies post-exposure prophylaxis can be difficult to predict and may be under-reported, particularly skin reactions. Doctors are concerned that severe reactions could create fear of rabies injections and prompt some people to delay or avoid prophylaxis.Doctors stress, however, that people bitten or scratched by a potentially rabid animal should not avoid recommended post-exposure prophylaxis. Patients should instead be counselled about possible reactions and have timely access to medical care if serious symptoms develop.The concern is greater in rural and poorly resourced areas, where access to specialist and emergency care may be limited. Doctors say the case underlines the need for better reporting of adverse reactions and timely access to treatment when complications occur.

Within seven days, he developed a skin rash that progressed to severe hives (urticaria) and angioedema, causing sudden swelling of the face, lips and throat. His condition later worsened with breathing difficulty, requiring specialist dermatological intervention.

NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has made an “interim safety recommendation” the Directorate General of Civil Aviation urgently “take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance” in its preliminary report into the probe of the severe turbulence on Air India’s Phuket-Delhi flight AI 2379 on Aug 4, 2026. While the probe is still on, the prelim report officially confirms that the “confirmatory (dope) test report of the pilot-in-command (PIC) was found non-negative” and that the Airbus A320 had suffered an extremely rare multiple hydraulic failure.When the “event” occurred, “initially, (the aircraft) gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet…. seat belt signs were off. Consequently, some passengers and cabin crew suffered injuries,” the report says. The “event’s” impact on the aircraft cabin damage was such that a “lavatory commode was uprooted from its original location.”The report says in its conclusion: “Detailed investigation regarding technical and other aspects are underway. In this case, it has been observed that the PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory test. The confirmation of use of psycho-active substances is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority.The preliminary report is published as per ICAO guidelines. The investigation is in progress. The final report will be published in due course.”The final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an A320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds — whether it happened due to something going wrong with the hardware or software or due to some manual intervention.“At 04:02:43 UTC, while cruising at flight level 36,000 feet, the aircraft’s flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of green hydraulic system. Further, at 04:02:47 UTC, the flight control system detected loss of blue and yellow hydraulic systems. At 04:02:48 UTC, the autopilot got disengaged and a continuous repetitive chime (CRC) came. At 04:02:51 UTC, the Stall warning triggered for 2 seconds.”“The co-pilot, who was the pilot flying (PF), responded and tried to control the prevailing situation. Subsequently, PIC took over the controls. Meanwhile, the aircraft encountered an altitude upset. Initially, it gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet during the event. At around 04:02:52 UTC, the blue hydraulic system was recovered, and few seconds later, the yellow hydraulic and the green hydraulic systems were also recovered. Consequently, this led to the recovery of the flight control surfaces. Subsequently, the aircraft operation returned to its normal operating condition,” says the report.The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the "muscles" that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheels. The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the “muscles” that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheelsThe cabin supervisor (head cabin crew) apprised the cockpit about the injuries suffered by the passengers and cabin crew. The flight crew assessed the cabin situation and took the decision to continue the flight to its destination, Delhi and not divert to the nearest en route airport.The aircraft cabin suffered significant damage during the “event”. The overhead ceiling panel was found cracked or deformed at various places. Most of the passenger service unit (PSU) panels were found dislocated or bent at various places. The overhead handrail was found broken, and the sealing panel was found dislocated near the 10th row. The forward right-side emergency exit handle was found broken.In a statement, Air India said: “We acknowledge the release of the preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) and continue to extend our full cooperation to the investigation, including providing access to all relevant operational, maintenance and technical records. Safety remains Air India's highest priority. Our pilots undergo rigorous training, regular proficiency checks, medical examinations and other regulatory assessments in accordance with applicable national and international requirements.Following the incident, Air India has started voluntary testing of 100% of its pilots as a further step to reinforce its safety-first approach.”“The airline maintains zero tolerance for any breach of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements and will take appropriate action wherever warranted. Air India remains committed to implementing any recommendations arising from the investigation,” AI said.
Article Summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has made an “interim safety recommendation” the Directorate General of Civil Aviation urgently “take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance” The preliminary report into the probe of the severe turbulence on Air India’s Phuket-Delhi flight AI 2379 on Aug 4, 2026.

Article Title: Smoking raises death risk by 55% in people with diabetes, global experts call for active quit treatment
Article Text:
A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes, according to evidence reviewed in a new international consensus that calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type 2 diabetes care. The experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-up instead of being given a one-time “quit smoking” warning.The recommendations, published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, are the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type 2 diabetes. They were developed by 35 experts from 13 countries, including Indian diabetes specialist Dr Anoop Misra.The consensus recommends varenicline as the first-line medicine where available, with nicotine replacement therapy or bupropion as alternatives when varenicline is unavailable or unsuitable. Medicines should be combined with structured, intensive behavioural support and repeated contact rather than brief counselling alone.The stronger approach reflects the added risk smoking poses in diabetes. A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.Doctors should review patients within two weeks of quitting and again at four weeks, checking blood sugar, weight, blood pressure and medicines, as quitting can alter drug metabolism and sometimes require dose adjustments.Weight gain, a common concern, should not deter quitting. In a US cohort of 10,809 people with type 2 diabetes, median weight gain within six years of quitting was 3.2 kg. Long-term quitters had lower all-cause mortality than continuing smokers regardless of weight gain, with mortality hazard ratios of 0.69, 0.57 and 0.51 for no gain, up to 5 kg and more than 5 kg gain, respectively.Smoking is also linked to kidney damage in diabetes, with higher risks of albuminuria and diabetic nephropathy. A Japanese study of 2,490 people with type 2 diabetes found insulin resistance rose with cigarettes smoked per day and fell with time after quitting.Quitting, however, can be difficult. Some patients may not recognise the link between smoking and diabetes complications, while others fear weight gain or use cigarettes to cope with stress and anxiety. The experts recommend personalised quit strategies and relapse prevention.The consensus also highlights gaps in diabetes care, where smoking cessation often remains limited to brief advice. It calls for routine smoking assessment, active treatment, metabolic monitoring and relapse prevention as part of diabetes care.
Article Summary: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes. A new international consensus calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type 2 diabetes care. The experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-up.

Article Title: Cruise tourism gets a boost as govt clears e-group visa
Article Text:
The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel (Representative Image)

NEW DELHI: As the govt focuses on positioning India as a leading global cruise destination, the home ministry has introduced e-group visit visa (cruise) for foreign tourists arriving in India on cruise vessels which follow a fixed and predetermined itinerary.The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel. The latter will authorise the foreign nationals arriving on cruise ships to enter India from any of the 38 designated e-visa enabled seaports. The e-group visit visa (cruise) will have a validity of 30 days and allow multiple entry.The cruise operator or agent of the vessel will need to submit the application for e-group visit visa for international passengers via the specified portal or mobile app, three days before berthing of the vessel at the first Indian port. No fresh application will be accepted beyond this cut-off.There is no limit on the number of tourists allowed on an e-group visit visa (cruise), home ministry sources told TOI. The details of the foreign passengers — name, nationality, passport number and issue/expiry date, etc — can be uploaded in bulk on the specified portal ( indianvisaonline.gov ) or mobile app.The e-group visit visa shall contain a QR code. Passengers may use this QR code at immigration checkpoints at the port of entry and for further travel within India, as per the fixed cruise itinerary.“Easier visa and immigration procedures will encourage international cruise companies to include Indian ports in their itineraries. This will also generate wider economic benefits for ports, hotels, restaurants, transport operators, touring businesses and local communities,” said an MHA official.The govt has, since 2024, launched two major initiatives to boost cruise tourism in India, given the great potential that the country’s 7,500-km coastline and a network of 110 navigable waterways connecting 400 rivers, presents, as per a PIB statement issued in April last year. The first initiative is Cruise Bharat Mission, launched in September 2024 with the aim of doubling the cruise traffic in India by 2029 (from 4.7 lakh in 2024 to almost 10 lakh in 2029). Also, the Maritime India Vision 2030 aims to make the country a significant player in the global cruise market, covering oceanic and coastal cruises, island and infrastructure development and river and inland cruises.
Article Summary: The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel. The visa will authorise the foreign nationals arriving on cruise ships to enter India from any of the 38 designated e-visa enabled seaports. There is no limit on the number of tourists allowed on an e- group visit visa.

Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5 million nonprofit faces scrutiny after records show $469,000 spent on management and $446,000 on charity
Article Text:
Travis Kelce(Image via Getty Images)

Travis Kelce nonprofit spending comes under scrutiny

Travis Kelce foundation says tax filings were incorrect

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Earlier this year, Travis Kelce ’s reputation for giving back was facing a setback after an investigation into the NFL players’ charitable foundations raised questions about how some donated money was spent. Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation raised more than $1.5 million between 2021 and 2024, yet its reported charity spending was notably lower than that of several other NFL-linked organizations.In January, 2026, according to federal tax records examined by The Arizona Republic, Eighty-Seven and Running reported about $1.5 million in revenue during the three-year period and roughly $1.1 million in expenses. About $446,000 was listed under charitable spending, while $469,000 was reported as management costs.That works out to about 41 cents of every dollar spent going toward charity based on the filings. Charity Navigator generally views nonprofits spending at least 70 cents of each dollar on programs as efficient, while CharityWatch uses 75 cents as a benchmark for high efficiency.The figures have drawn attention partly because of the foundation's ties to A&A Management Group.The company was co-founded by Travis Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and André Eanes. Aaron Eanes also serves as the nonprofit’s executive director.Laurie Styron, executive director of CharityWatch, raised concerns about the structure after reviewing the records.“It appears to function more as an extension of the management company versus as an independent public charity,” said Laurie Styron, the executive director of CharityWatch, an independent charity watchdog group that reviewed the nonprofit’s tax filings for The Arizona Republic.“That’s not how charities work. It’s wrong.”..Travis Kelce’s team disputes the picture presented by the filings. Aaron Eanes said the reported figures did not properly classify some operational expenses tied to charitable work.“Operational costs for charitable efforts were “mistakenly reported under management rather than allocated adequately to program services,” Eanes told The Republic, so the public records do not provide an accurate “indication of where the resources were truly directed.”.Eanes said the foundation has since changed its approach, adding that management fees fell sharply in 2024 and reached zero in 2025. He also said the organization plans to expand its board, bring in nonprofit advisers and improve its reporting practices.“Looking ahead, we are expanding our board of directors, bringing on advisers with nonprofit expertise, and restructuring our reporting processes to better reflect our actual program work. We are dedicated to ensuring this foundation operates at the highest standards.”The scrutiny comes as the NFL continues to highlight charitable work through the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year program. Kelce has been nominated three times and has supported causes in both Kansas City and his hometown of Cleveland.Kelce's foundation’s reported numbers do not erase that community work, but they do highlight why financial transparency matters. For celebrity-led nonprofits, public trust depends not only on how much money is raised, but also on how clearly and responsibly that money reaches the people it is meant to help.The foundation has since said it took steps to address the accounting and governance concerns, including changing how expenses were reported and eliminating management fees in 2025. However, there has been no public indication that the concerns raised by CharityWatch and The Arizona Republic have been formally cleared or independently resolved
Article Summary: Travis Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation raised more than $1.5 million between 2021 and 2024, yet its reported charity spending was notably lower than that of several other NFL-linked organizations. The figures have drawn attention partly because of the foundation's ties to A&A Management Group. The foundation has since said it took steps to address the accounting and governance concerns.

Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday released the ‘RAKSHA’ document on defence diplomacy, outlining India's strategic roadmap and vision for expanding global defence partnerships over the next 10 years.The document, unveiled at a special event in New Delhi, lays out a framework aimed at aligning India's national security objectives with proactive international cooperation, according to the ministry of defence.The strategic blueprint focuses on deepening bilateral and multilateral security ties, building capacity with friendly countries, promoting indigenous defence exports and strengthening maritime security.The ‘RAKSHA’ framework is built around four key pillars:The ministry of defence said the document provides a “clear, actionable vision” for the next decade as defence of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and secretary (defence production) Sanjeev Kumar were among the senior officials present at the event.Secretary (east) in pillar of the country's foreign policy.The release came a day after India and Belgium held extensive discussions aimed at expanding bilateral defence and industrial cooperation.Singh hosted Belgian defence and trade minister Theo Francken in New Delhi on Wednesday, with multiple memorandums of understanding and contracts signed under defence industrial cooperation.“Had a very productive meeting with the Defence and Trade Minister of Belgium, Mr @FranckenTheo, in New Delhi today.
