Article Summary: The document lays out a framework aimed at aligning India's national security objectives with proactive international cooperation. It focuses on deepening bilateral and multilateral security ties, building capacity with friendly countries, promoting indigenous defence exports and strengthening maritime security. The document was officially released during an event at Kartavya Bhawan.

Article Title: Aravalis can’t be defined by height or any single criterion: SC panel
Article Text:
Asks For 6 More Months To Frame Recommendations





GURGAON: The high-powered committee (HPC) tasked with defining Aravalis has informed Supreme Court that its complex landscape cannot be captured through a single terrain or height-based criterion and sought six more months till Feb 27 to complete the exercise.HPC was formed by Supreme Court after an environment ministry panel’s definition, which recognised as Aravalis only hills that had an elevation of 100 metres or more and was adopted by the court last Nov, drew widespread protests, particularly in Rajasthan . The court stayed its judgement in Dec and subsequently set up the HPC in May this year.In its compliance report submitted to SC, HPC said geospatial analysis, field validation, expert examination and stakeholder consultations are needed before it can submit its final recommendations. Defining the ancient, and in parts severely degraded, ranges that run between Gujarat and Delhi isn’t an easy task because the Aravalis lack uniformity. At the same time, any restrictive definition could leave ecologically connected hills, forests, aquifers and other important landscapes outside the protection framework, affecting the ecology of the northern plains and making Delhi-NCR more vulnerable to dust storms.HPC, which is led by 1991-batch IFS officer and director-general of Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education Kanchan Devi, was originally asked to submit its report by Aug 31.“The work undertaken so far has evidenced the breadth, scientific complexity and wider implications of the issues requiring examination,” HPC said in its report. It added that the questions before it “cannot appropriately be addressed through a single terrain-based criterion or a single source of evidence”.The panel said it was, therefore, bringing together spatial, ecological, geological, hydrological, socio-economic and stakeholder evidence. The panel is considering an Aravali Ecosystem Landscape framework under which the range would be assessed as more than a collection of hills and ridges.The approach will consider geological and geomorphological features, terrain, watersheds, hydrological systems, forests, biodiversity and ecological connectivity. It will also include recorded forests, protected areas, wetlands, critical catchments, groundwater recharge areas, sacred sites, traditional pastures and areas of archaeological significance.The committee said the Aravalis need to be understood “through multiple interrelated dimensions”.Its field assessment from Aug 6-11 reinforced this approach, with the panel saying it found Aravalis to be, in large parts, “a connected landscape with interlinked ecological, hydrological, biodiversity and socio-cultural values”.HPC is also examining the impact of mining, stone quarrying, stone crushing and unregulated sand mining on drainage systems, topography, water systems and biodiversity. It has so far received 680 representations from farmers, local communities, mining sector stakeholders, residents, civil society groups and govt bodies.Former forest conservator of south Haryana RP Balwan, who had moved Supreme Court against the ministry panel’s 100m definition, said the geological origin of the range makes a height or gap-based definition problematic.“The Aravali range was formed by tectonic compression during ancient plate collisions. The gaps and height of the range are immaterial. For example, the Himalayas are one irrespective of the political boundary. Aravalis should be considered as one ecosystem,” he said.
Article Summary: High-powered committee (HPC) tasked with defining Aravalis has sought six more months till Feb 27 to complete the exercise. Defining the ancient, and in parts severely degraded, ranges that run between Gujarat and Delhi isn’t an easy task. HPC was formed by Supreme Court after an environment ministry panel’s definition drew widespread protests.

Article Title: From 2-year stay to 12-year wait: Delhi’s Kathputli Colony families await homes
Article Text:
Thousands of families displaced from Kathputli Colony await permanent homes after twelve years.

TOI





NEW DELHI: Thousands of families are still waiting at Anand Parbat, 12 years after being moved out of Kathputli Colony with the promise they would be given permanent homes.What was meant to be a temporary stay of two years at Anand Parbat has stretched into more than a decade, with the families now living in a rapidly deteriorating transit camp and their dream of owning a home once again fading.Delhi Development Authority (DDA) shifted the families to Anand Parbat in 2014 as part of its first in-situ rehabilitation project under the ‘Jahan Jhuggi Wahan Makan’ initiative. The project was planned on a public-private partnership (PPP) model through a private developer and was expected to be completed within two years.These people, many of whom traditionally worked as puppeteers, magicians, kalandars and acrobats and largely belonged to the Bhat community of Rajasthan, have since spent years waiting for rehabilitation.The same situation continues even as Master Plan of Delhi 2047 explicitly prioritises in-situ slum rehabilitation projects, offering increased FAR for PPP projects.The history of Kathputli Colony goes back to 1959, when tribal communities from villages in Rajasthan began settling on vacant land near what is now Shadipur depot. Later, street performers from Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra joined them. Since their professions required frequent travel and access to public transport, they began seeking permanent housing in the late 1960s.DDA announced an in-situ rehabilitation project for them in 2009. A transit camp was developed by the private developer in 2013 to accommodate around 2,800 families at Anand Parbat while permanent houses for them were to be constructed at Kathputli Colony.Raheja Developers Ltd began work, but a portion of the land was still encroached upon. “Full-fledged work began only in 2021 after a court gave its decision in favour of DDA. The agreement was for developing a transit camp, but there was no mention of its maintenance. In 2022, DDA promised to pay maintenance charges, but nothing happened,” said an office-bearer with the developer.Raheja didn’t provide its official response despite repeated attempts byMeanwhile, the transit camp has deteriorated. Residents complain of leaking roofs, damaged flooring, leaking water pipes and poorly maintained toilets. They say the temporary structures, designed to last only two years, were never meant to become their homes for over a decade.Patasi, president of the RWA of the transit camp and one of its first occupants, said several politicians and officials visited the residents and the construction site over the years, but the promised flats remained elusive.“Look at the condition we are living in. The roofs leak so badly that we have to use utensils and buckets to collect the water. Recently, a boy fractured his shoulder after a portion of a roof collapsed. The condition of the toilets is deplorable. Water pipes are leaking and the concrete flooring is damaged,” she said.“Residents interacted with former MoHUA minister Hardeep Puri earlier and Union minister Manohar Lal Khattar around six months ago, and were assured each time that the flats will be transferred soon.”While DDA vice-chairman N Saravana Kumar claimed that sanitation was fine at the transit camp, it recently invited tender of approx Rs 5.5 crore for sanitation and sweeping services.For Pappu, who lives in a 10x10-foot transit unit with a family of 16, including his three sons, their wives and grandchildren, the prolonged wait has become a symbol of their poverty. “If we had money, why would we live in such circumstances? Our poverty has been mocked by everyone. We have had to divide the small space with curtains,” he said.Vinod Bhat, another resident, questioned why govt and elected representatives remained silent while the developer continued to maintain the transit camp.Another office-bearer at the developer’s office in the transit camp said, “The maintenance and services provided by the developer include cleaning around 900 toilets, operating a 50,000-litre RO system, garbage collection, road sweeping, electrical and plumbing repairs, maintenance of the transit units and sewage treatment plant. DDA only provides the water supply.” The maintenance bill, she claimed, has now run into crores of rupees.Sources said DDA held a meeting with the developer in mid-July. “It was decided that the authority would pay within 15 days the developer’s maintenance charges for the complex for 12 years. The developer will then complete the pending work and hand over the complex to DDA within three months,” the sources said.Residents said a DDA engineer met them in July and assured them that outstanding issues had been resolved and the project would move ahead.DDA, however, has a different take. Its vice-chairman said the developer had been served several notices to complete the project but didn’t respond. “We are waiting for some time and, if we do not get a satisfactory response, we will be forced to take strict action,” he said.The officials didn’t deny the possibility of exercising the option of engaging another developer to finish the project. Till then, the wait for the hapless thousands goes on.
Article Summary: Delhi Development Authority (DDA) shifted the families to Anand Parbat in 2014 as part of its first in-situ rehabilitation project. The project was planned on a public-private partnership (PPP) model through a private developer and was expected to be completed within two years.

Article Title: ‘No record’: Podcaster’s claim reignites row over CJP founder’s BU degree; Dipke hits back with video
Article Text:
A controversy has resurfaced regarding Abhijeet Dipke's educational credentials from Boston University

Sonam Wangchuk on Dipke’s political ambitions





NEW DELHI: A fresh controversy has erupted over Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke’s educational credentials after podcaster Prakhar Gupta said one of his friends who studied at Boston University could not find a record of Dipke’s graduation there.The claim was made during an episode of The Prakhar Gupta Xperience podcast featuring climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.Gupta said one of his close friends had studied at Boston University and had been actively involved in supporting the CJP-led protest at Jantar Mantar.“One of my best friends went to Boston University. It is also Abhijeet’s college,” Gupta said during the podcast.He said his friend had participated in the protests and produced media content in support of the movement.Gupta claimed that about a month later, his friend began looking into Dipke’s educational credentials and allegedly found no record of him graduating from Boston University.“He has gone down the rabbit hole of checking up Abhijeet’s education credentials and found there is no record of him graduating from Boston University,” Gupta said.Dipke, however, responded to the claim on X, appearing to mock the suggestion that his graduation could not be verified.“Not my fault that his friends were not invited at BU COM Grad events,” Dipke wrote, while sharing a video appearing to show him at an event associated with Boston University’s College of Communication graduate community.The video was a screen recording of a story posted by an Instagram account identified as “BU COM Grad, Student Council”.The latest allegation comes despite Boston University itself having published material identifying Dipke as a graduate.In a June 2026 article, Boston University’s College of Communication described Dipke as a “COM grad” and said he had completed his master’s in public relations from the university the previous year.The university article also carried an interview with Dipke in which he discussed how his studies at BU influenced the communication strategy behind the CJP campaign.Dipke has previously maintained that he studied at Boston University and earned a master’s degree in public relations. He has also said his education was financed through a Boston University scholarship and an education loan.Amid the controversy, Dipke had earlier said he was willing to produce his degree and other documents to establish his educational credentials.The dispute has now resurfaced as Dipke and the CJP leadership face increasing scrutiny over their backgrounds and political ambitions following the movement’s prolonged protests over examination-related issues.The same podcast also featured Wangchuk discussing Dipke and other CJP organisers, including their possible political ambitions.Wangchuk said he believed Dipke and his fellow organisers appeared to have political aspirations, although they had not explicitly told him about any such plans. He said there was nothing inherently wrong with political ambitions as long as the CJP remained a non-party platform.“Political ambition is very normal,” Wangchuk said, adding that he did not care about the organisers’ past political connections and had no problem with their present or future political aspirations.Wangchuk also said the organisers were not necessarily acting entirely selflessly and described them as “well meaning”, “quite skilled” and “above average”. He cautioned that their political aspirations should not turn the CJP platform itself into a vehicle for any political party.He said the organisers could eventually join an existing political party or form one of their own, but should preserve CJP as a “neutral, apolitical pressure group”.The comments came days before the Supreme Court quashed 127 FIRs filed against student protesters in five states in connection with the CJP agitation.Following assurances given before the court, CJP called off its proposed September 5 march from India Gate to Delhi Police headquarters.
Article Summary: A fresh controversy has erupted over Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's educational credentials. Podcaster Prakhar Gupta said one of his friends who studied at Boston University could not find a record of Dipke’s graduation there. The claim was made during an episode of The PrakHar Gupta Xperience podcast featuring climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.

Article Title: ‘Floor-collected, broken noodles used to make bhujia': What FSSAI found at Wai-Wai's Rajasthan unit
Article Text:
India's food regulator FSSAI has ordered CG Foods India to stop producing veg bhujia





NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has directed CG Foods India Pvt Ltd to stop production of its ‘Veg Bhujia Namkeen’ after an inspection at the company’s facility in Rajasthan found multiple food safety and hygiene violations.The food regulator said on Thursday that enforcement action had been initiated against the company over “unsafe processing, unlicensed bhujia manufacturing, and predated packaging”.During an inspection at the company’s unit in Roopangarh, Ajmer, officials found floor-collected and broken noodles being reprocessed into bhujia without heat treatment, FSSAI said.The inspection also uncovered the use of predated packaging and the unlicensed manufacture of ‘Wai-Wai MaMa’ and ‘Wai-Wai Mama Punte’ bhujia variants, allegedly in violation of Section 31(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.FSSAI said officials seized 32,107.2 kg of stock, including loose broken noodles, from the premises.The inspection further revealed deficiencies in hygiene and documentation, including inadequate pest-control records and other food safety lapses.Officials collected samples for laboratory testing and detained 1,925 boxes of expired finished products. Legal proceedings have also been initiated against the company.FSSAI directed CG Foods India to discontinue production of Veg Bhujia Namkeen products without the required approvals and corrective measures.The regulator said further action would be taken based on the laboratory test results and findings of the inspection.
Article Summary: India's food regulator FSSAI has ordered CG Foods India to stop producing veg bhujia. The food regulator said on Thursday that enforcement action had been initiated against the company over “unsafe processing, unlicensed bhuJia manufacturing, and predated packaging”

Article Title: Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is launching a defense technology company backed by Palantir
Article Text:
Alex Karp backed defense company turning wartime experience into a product

A war reshaping military technology

Fedorov's abrupt exit from government

What Fedorov has been doing since leaving government

Palantir CEO Alex Karp stepping in as the first lead investor in a new defense technology company founded by former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedoro. According to a report by CNBC, the size of Karp’s investment has not been disclosed, but Fedorov’s press office confirmed the partnership, saying details of cooperation with Palantir will be announced gradually. In a video posted by Fedorov on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Karp praised the venture, saying it could bring Ukraine’s wartime knowledge and experience “as a product to allied countries.” He added: “You and your colleagues are launching a company that I think will be defining for the world.”The company’s name, specific technologies, and the extent of Karp’s involvement have not yet been disclosed. Palantir did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Fedorov’s office said the venture will build on lessons learned during Ukraine’s war with Russia, where drones, artificial intelligence, and battlefield software have played a critical role.The launch comes as Ukraine's ongoing war with Russia continues to accelerate the development and battlefield deployment of technologies including drones, artificial intelligence, and military software.Fedorov, long known as a vocal advocate for using technology to modernize Ukraine's military, said the new company would apply lessons learned during the war to build technology usable by both Ukraine and its allied partners.Fedorov, 35, said in a statement: “During the full-scale war, our team gained unique experience working with defense technologies in Ukraine and seeing firsthand how technology is transforming modern warfare.” He added that the company will aim to apply those lessons to products usable by both Ukraine and its allies.Fedorov, 35, was removed from his role as defense minister by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in July as part of a broader government reshuffle, after serving in the position for just six months. His removal sparked public protests in Ukraine at the time.Since exiting government, Fedorov has been actively courting US investors and technology executives as he pursues a series of defense-focused ventures. He is separately seeking U.S. backing for a defense technology investment fund targeting areas including battlefield robotics, interceptor drones, and AI-enabled missile systems, according to a Financial Times report published last week.Fedorov built relationships with several prominent U.S. tech executives during the war. Last month, he described Elon Musk as the most important tech figure and entrepreneur in the world for Ukraine, crediting Starlink's decision to block Russian forces from accessing the satellite internet service.
Article Summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp is the first lead investor in a new defense technology company founded by former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedoro. Fedorov's office said the venture will build on lessons learned during Ukraine’s war with Russia, where drones, artificial intelligence, and battlefield software have played a critical role.

Article Title: Read Mayor Zohran Mamdani's statement as New York bans AI in Elementary and Middle Schools; says: Tech industry wants us to believe ...
Article Text:
Read Mayor Zohran Mamdani's statement as New York bans AI in Elementary and Middle Schools

Mayor Zohran Mamdani says AI in early education is not necessary

What New York's AI school rules mean for students

New York schools face questions over AI-powered apps

New York City is putting strict limits on AI in public schools, with younger students facing the biggest restrictions. According to a report by New York Times, about 600,000 students, or roughly two-thirds of the city’s public school population, will not be allowed to use AI until they reach high school, while AI use in high school will be limited to specific cases. As per the report, the policy is also placing new limits on digital devices and screen time. No individual screens will be allowed for students until third grade, while middle school students could face a recommended screen-time limit of 45 minutes a day. AI-powered companion chatbots designed to provide emotional or mental support will also be banned across all grades.New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the city does not accept the idea that AI must become part of early education. “The tech industry wants us to believe that A.I.-powered early education is not only inevitable, but necessary. We do not see it that way,” Mamdani said in a statement as quoted in the report."I am proud to announce New York City's first-ever comprehensive AI policy for our public schools, City Hall's answer to those questions. It is the most comprehensive of its kind anywhere in the country, and it begins with a simple principle: Children need their teachers and human connection in order to learn and in order to grow.And they need to develop skills alongside their peers, build relationships with their teachers, and wrestle with tough problems on their own. The tech industry wants us to believe that AI in early education is not only inevitable but that it is necessary. We do not see it that way. I have yet to see a study showing that AI is beneficial for students in elementary and middle school, with the exception, of course, of research sponsored by the very corporations that stand to profit. So, beginning this school year, we will implement a one-year moratorium on generative AI for students in 2-K through eighth grade," Mamdani said.Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels also said the city would not treat more technology as the same thing as innovation.“We’re putting guardrails in place to protect the critical human connection, curiosity, and creativity that help children grow,” he said.Under the new policy, AI will generally be off limits for elementary and middle school students until they enter high school. High school students will be allowed to use AI in certain situations. The rules also address how teachers can use AI. Teachers will be allowed to use AI for tasks such as creating lesson plans, translating materials and writing messages.However, AI cannot be used to make certain important decisions about students. For example, teachers cannot use AI to decide whether a student should graduate or determine how to counsel a student experiencing a crisis.The rules also include exceptions for some technology. Centrally approved instructional programs, including e-books and coding software, will not be covered by the restrictions. Some testing tools and technology designed to support students with disabilities or those learning English will also be exempt.As stated in the NYT report, the policy could also affect educational apps already used in schools, particularly as more software companies add generative AI features to their products. Naveed Hasan, a member of a city education oversight panel, questioned how the rules would work when AI is becoming part of many software products.The city education system has a budget of about $40 billion, giving it significant purchasing power when dealing with technology companies. Hasan said the department could potentially use that influence to push companies to change how their educational apps work.
Article Summary: New York City is putting strict limits on AI in public schools, with younger students facing the biggest restrictions. About 600,000 students, or roughly two-thirds of the city’s public school population, will not be allowed to use AI until they reach high school. The policy is also placing new limits on digital devices and screen time.

Article Title: US government now 'trusts' Anthropic, the company that it banned months ago; Howard Lutnick says: They are back on ...
Article Text:
Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown played key role in diplomatic turnaround

In what can be called a major diplomatic reversal following months of bitter friction over artificial intelligence (AI) safety protocols and national defense boundaries, the Trump administration officially trusts Anthropic, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick confirmed this week. Speaking in an interview with Axios, Lutnick responded to a direct question whether he places confidence in Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.“We trust Anthropic. They've done what we asked. They're back on the right side. So the answer is: Yes,” Lutnick responded. The remarks signal a major de-icing of ties that earlier this year resulted in sweeping export restrictions targeting Anthropic's most capable foundation models. As per the report, personal friction between top officials and corporate leaders had also compounded those clashes, driving the firm away from executive favour.The report says that the turnaround in relations arrived after Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown assumed a central role in managing the startup’s relationship with Washington. Lutnick showcased the improved alliance by personally introducing Brown before a global audience of dignitaries at the G20 Innovation Ministerial, inviting the co-founder to tell his story on the international stage, the report noted.In behind-the-scenes diplomacy, Brown proved critical in mending fences across official channels, reportedly conducting extensive bilateral discussions with Lutnick and National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross.Taking the ministerial stage, Brown openly commended a Truth Social post shared by President Donald Trump praising data center expansion. Brown highlighted that advanced facilities generate tax revenues, create employment and are engineered to inject new electrical capacity into the grid.The shift comes amid shifting courtroom battles over prior regulatory crackdowns. A federal judge recently struck down the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic as a supply-chain hazard, determining that the punitive designation infringed upon the technology company’s constitutional protections.Anthropic is continuing to litigate an additional Pentagon designation invoked under a different statute before the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit.
Article Summary: Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown played key role in diplomatic turnaround. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick confirmed this week that he places confidence in Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. The remarks signal a major de-icing of ties that earlier this year resulted in sweeping export restrictions.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai sends a message to his college IIT Kharagpur as it celebrates 75 years; shares happy memories as student: Meals at Harry's, studying in…
Article Text:
Image credit: Instagram

Sundar Pichai's IIT Kharagpur memories: Harry's, Illu and room B-308

Pichai's AI prediction: from labs to farmers, doctors and government offices

IIT Kharagpur at 75: why Pichai is betting on students

Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has recorded a video message for IIT Kharagpur as the institute turns 75, and he spends most of it on the small stuff. Meals at Harry's. The Illu festival. Nights spent studying in room B-308. The wingmates, and the professors who stuck with him. Campus, he said, is also where he met his wife Anjali, where he first learned to program, and where he carried floppy disks around to get time on one of the few machines available. "These moments shaped the course of my life," he said, "putting me on a path to Google."That last line is the pivot. The message, posted by IIT Kharagpur on X, works as two things at once—a nostalgia reel and a forecast. Pichai, who graduated in 1993 with a B.Tech in metallurgical engineering, uses the anniversary to set out where he thinks artificial intelligence lands over the next five years, and to make a case that universities, not just tech companies, will decide whether any of it reaches people who aren't already using it.The specificity is what makes it land. B-308 in Nehru Hall is an unremarkable hostel room—bed, study table, chair, almirah—and it has quietly become a campus landmark, currently occupied by a final-year chemical engineering student.Metallurgy, meanwhile, sits nowhere near the top of India's engineering pecking order, which is part of why the room has the pull it does.Pichai called an education from the institute "truly a gift" and said IIT Kharagpur "played a formative role in shaping the lens through which I strive to make an impact on the world." He also noted how far its graduates have travelled, in India and outside it.The forward-looking half is the newsier one. "When I look at the next five years, I see AI moving away from the lab and the early adopters and into the hands of people doing the work," Pichai said—"the healthcare workers, the government officials, the farmers, developers, and entrepreneurs."The framing is deliberate. He is not describing AI as something to experiment with, but as something that sits inside jobs people already do. "We are building AI so that it can help all of us do our work at the next level and do it in a more fulfilling way," he added.It also tracks with where Alphabet has pointed itself. Under Pichai, AI now runs through Search, Cloud and the Gemini family of models a shift the company's own regulatory filings describe as central to its strategy. A prediction about AI spreading into everyday work is, conveniently, also a description of Google's product roadmap.On India, Pichai said the country is increasingly producing innovations that can benefit the whole world, and that an "ambitious, optimistic new generation of Indians" has the chance to reimagine what's possible. AI can amplify that potential, he argued, but universities are what keep it useful to everyone rather than to a narrow few—a point that doubles as the institute's brief for its next 25 years.Much of the current momentum, he said, is coming from students. He recalled meeting Gemini Student Ambassadors from across India at the AI Impact Summit in Delhi this year: "Their enthusiasm for how technology can improve lives was palpable, and it's why I'm so optimistic about the future." The role of IIT Kharagpur, he added, "will only grow in importance as you lead the next wave of technology."The institute responded by calling the message a reflection of "the enduring global impact of the IIT ecosystem," saying it now looks ahead "to nurture ideas, inspire generations and create solutions that make a difference to India and the world."After Kharagpur, Pichai went to Stanford and then Wharton. He joined Google in 2004, worked on Toolbar and Chrome before taking charge of product and engineering across its major platforms, became CEO in 2015, and added Alphabet in December 2019.
Article Summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has recorded a video message for IIT Kharagpur as the institute turns 75. He uses the anniversary to set out where he thinks artificial intelligence lands over the next five years. The message works as two things at once—a nostalgia reel and a forecast.

Article Title: Amazon to hire 160,000 temporary workers this festive season
Article Text:
Amazon rejects allegations of consumer harm

Ahead of the upcoming festive season, Amazon India has announced that it has created more than 160,000 seasonal work opportunities across its pan India operations network that supports its ecommerce and quick commerce business. These include direct and indirect work opportunities across 400 cities in India, spanning large metros as well as tier 2 and 3 cities like Varanasi, Kochi, Jalandhar, Ghaziabad, Ranchi, Salem, Gorakhpur, and others. Amazon has created opportunities for thousands of women and associates with disabilities in its network. The new associates will join Amazon’s existing pan-India operations network helping pick, pack, ship, and deliver customer orders safely and reliably while supporting the growing demand during the festive period. Amazon has already onboarded the majority of these associates in preparation for the festive season and has begun providing them with the necessary training.As part of Amazon’s commitment to supporting its associates, even the seasonal associates will have access to the range of safety and welfare programs and benefits that other associates have. This includes benefits like a safe, supportive and inclusive workplace, safety, financial and social security.Through its Samridhi program, Amazon will also support associates joining the company’s operations network ahead of the festive season to enroll on the e-shram portal and access other government welfare and social security programs.“We are committed to providing customers across every pin-code in India with fast and reliable deliveries this festive season. To meet the anticipated increase in customer demand, we have created over 1.6 lakh seasonal work opportunities across our operations network. As we focus on building one of India’s largest, safest, fastest and most reliable operations network, we are also committed to building an inclusive workforce, with opportunities for thousands of women associates and persons with disabilities. This expanded workforce will help us strengthen our fulfillment and logistics capabilities and ensure we can handle the festive season seamlessly. Many of these associates continue their journey with Amazon beyond the festive period, while several others return year after year to work with us,” said Abhinav Singh, VP, Operations, Amazon India, APAC, Middle East, Africa and Turkiye.Amazon India claims to have fulfilment centers spread across 15 states, offering over 43 million cubic feet of storage space for seller inventory; sortation centers in 19 states; along with a network of close to 2,000 Amazon-operated and partner delivery stations. Also, it has 28,000 'Hub delivery' partners and thousands of Amazon Flex partners, who are ready to deliver smiles to customers across the country.
Article Summary: Amazon India has created more than 160,000 seasonal work opportunities across its pan India operations network. The new associates will join Amazon’s existing pan-India operations network helping pick, pack, ship, and deliver customer orders. Amazon has already onboarded the majority of these associates in preparation for the festive season.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos: “I knew that if I failed I wouldn’t regret that, but…” - a lesson about risk, failure and regret
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos

“I knew that if I failed I wouldn’t regret that, but I knew the one thing I might regret is not trying.”

What Jeff Bezos meant by the quote

The modest beginnings behind a much bigger company

The long-term view behind a risky choice

Why failure mattered less to him than uncertainty

A lesson about decisions rather than ambition

Trying can be smaller than people think

Lessons to learn from Jeff Bezos’ quote

Failure is not always the worst outcome

Consider the cost of inaction

Think beyond the present moment

Regret can be a useful decision-making tool

Trying does not always mean taking a huge risk

Do not confuse uncertainty with failure

Security has a cost too

A decision does not need a guaranteed outcome to be worthwhile

Learn to separate fear from judgement

The goal is not to avoid every mistake

There are decisions that become difficult precisely because both choices carry a cost. Staying where things are familiar can offer security, while taking a chance can leave a person facing an outcome that cannot be predicted. Jeff Bezos encountered that dilemma in the 1990s, when he was working at the investment firm D. E. Shaw began considering an idea built around the rapidly expanding internet. Leaving a well-paid job for an online bookseller was hardly a guaranteed route to success. Bezos knew the business could fail. What mattered to him was a different possibility: that years later, he might look back and wish he had given the idea a chance. He eventually left his job and founded Amazon . The decision became one of the defining moments of his career, but the reasoning behind it came before anyone knew how the company would turn out.Bezos was describing the way he weighed the risk of leaving his established career. He did not know whether Amazon would succeed. In fact, he considered failure a realistic possibility.His thinking centred on regret rather than prediction. He imagined himself much older and considered how he might view the decision with the benefit of hindsight.If the business failed, he would at least know that he had attempted it. If he stayed in his job and never tried, there would be no answer to the question of what might have happened.The quote is therefore not simply about being unafraid of failure. It is about recognising that inaction can also have consequences. Sometimes the safest decision in the short term can leave a person with a longer-lasting question.It is easy to view the original Amazon through the scale of the company that exists today. That can distort what Bezos was actually deciding in 1994.Amazon did not begin as a plan to create a vast technology and retail company. It began as an online bookstore. The first version of the business was focused on selling books through a website at a time when buying something online was still unfamiliar to most people.The company opened its virtual doors in July 1995.Within its first weeks, Amazon had shipped books across the United States and to customers overseas. The catalogue also gave the business an advantage that physical shops struggled to match. It could offer a huge range of titles without having to keep every book on shelves.The early success did not prove that Bezos had known what would happen. It showed what happened after he decided to try.The phrase most closely associated with Bezos's decision is his “regret minimisation framework”.Rather than trying to predict every detail of the future, he imagined reaching old age and looking back at the choice. From that imagined future perspective, he considered which decision was more likely to cause regret. The framework simplified the problem. If Amazon failed, Bezos could return to the job market and continue with his career. If he never tried, he might spend years wondering whether the business could have worked.It was not a mathematical formula. It was a way of changing the time frame of the decision. A difficult choice in the present can look different when viewed from decades later.Failure produces an answer. If a business closes, a person knows that a particular approach did not work. If an application is rejected, there is a definite outcome. Even an unsuccessful project can reveal what needs to change.Not trying provides none of that. The possibility remains hypothetical. There is no evidence showing whether the idea could have succeeded or failed.For Bezos, that unresolved possibility was harder to accept than failure itself. That is perhaps the most precise way to understand the quote. He was not claiming that failure feels good. He was saying that failure was an outcome he could live with, while never making the attempt might leave a question that could not be settled.The quote can be applied without turning every difficult choice into an entrepreneurial gamble. A person considering a career change, a new qualification, a business idea or a creative project might ask a similar question: which outcome would be harder to live with years from now?Sometimes the responsible decision is to stay put. Financial obligations, family circumstances, timing and the consequences of failure all matter. Bezos's framework cannot account for every situation.What it can do is introduce another consideration into the decision, the cost of never finding out.There is also no need for “trying” to involve quitting a job or risking a life's savings.It might mean testing an idea on a small scale. Applying for an opportunity. Taking a course. Speaking to someone in an industry you are considering. Building a first version of a project before deciding whether to pursue it seriously.Those steps can reduce uncertainty without requiring an immediate leap. In that sense, the useful part of Bezos's thinking is not necessarily the size of the risk he took. It is the way he separated the fear of failure from the question of future regret.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos said he would not regret leaving his job to start Amazon. He did not know whether the business would succeed or not. He considered failure a realistic possibility rather than a prediction. He imagined himself much older and how he might view the decision with the benefit of hindsight.
